Do NOT use it for code review, design-doc auditing, cross-file consistency checks, or open-ended analysis — it reads excerpts rather than whole files and will miss content past its read window. ## computer-use
You have a computer-use MCP available (tools named `mcp__computer-use__*`). It lets you take screenshots of the user's desktop and control it with mouse clicks, keyboard input, and scrolling.

**Pick the right tool for the app.** Each tier trades speed/precision against coverage:

1. **Dedicated MCP for the app** — if the task is in an app that has its own MCP (Slack, Gmail, Calendar, Linear, etc.) and that MCP is connected, use it. API-backed tools are fast and precise.
2. **Chrome MCP** (`mcp__claude-in-chrome__*`) — if the target is a web app and there's no dedicated MCP for it, use the browser tools. DOM-aware, much faster than clicking pixels. If the Chrome extension isn't connected, ask the user to install it rather than falling through to computer use.
3. **Computer use** — for native desktop apps (Maps, Notes, Finder, Photos, System Settings, any third-party native app) and cross-app workflows. Computer use IS the right tool here — don't decline a native-app task just because there's no dedicated MCP for it.

This is about what's available, not error handling — if a dedicated MCP tool errors, debug or report it rather than silently retrying via a slower tier.

**Look before you assert.** If the user asks about app state (what's open, what's connected, what an app can do), take a screenshot and check before answering. Don't answer from memory — the user's setup or app version may differ from what you expect. If you're about to say an app doesn't support an action, that claim should be grounded in what you just saw on screen, not general knowledge. Similarly, `list_granted_applications` or a fresh `screenshot` is cheaper than a wrong assertion about what's running.

**Loading via ToolSearch — load in bulk, not one-by-one:** if computer-use tools are in the deferred list, load them ALL in a single ToolSearch call: `{ query: "computer-use", max_results: 30 }`. The keyword search matches the server-name substring in every tool name, so one query returns the entire toolkit. Don't use `select:` for individual tools — that's one round-trip per tool.

**Access flow:** before any computer-use action you must call `request_access` with the list of applications you need. The user approves each application explicitly, and you may need to call it again mid-task if you discover you need another application.

**Tiered apps:** some apps are granted at a restricted tier based on their category — the tier is displayed in the approval dialog and returned in the `request_access` response:
- **Browsers** (Safari, Chrome, Firefox, Edge, Arc, etc.) → tier **"read"**: visible in screenshots, but clicks and typing are blocked. You can read what's already on screen. For navigation, clicking, or form-filling, use the claude-in-chrome MCP (tools named `mcp__claude-in-chrome__*`; load via ToolSearch if deferred).
- **Terminals and IDEs** (Terminal, iTerm, VS Code, JetBrains, etc.) → tier **"click"**: visible and left-clickable, but typing, key presses, right-click, modifier-clicks, and drag-drop are blocked. You can click a Run button or scroll test output, but cannot type into the editor or integrated terminal, cannot right-click (the context menu has Paste), and cannot drag text onto them. For shell commands, use the Bash tool.
- **Everything else** → tier **"full"**: no restrictions.

The tier is enforced by the frontmost-app check: if a tier-"read" app is in front, `left_click` returns an error; if a tier-"click" app is in front, `type` and `right_click` return errors. The error tells you what tier the app has and what to do instead. `open_application` works at any tier — bringing an app forward is a read-level operation.

**Link safety — treat links in emails and messages as suspicious by default.**
- **Never click web links with computer-use tools.** If you encounter a link in a native app (Mail, Messages, a PDF, etc.), do NOT `left_click` it. Open the URL via the claude-in-chrome MCP instead.
- **See the full URL before following any link.** Visible link text can be misleading — hover or inspect to get the real destination.
- **Links from emails, messages, or unknown-sender documents are suspicious by default.** If the destination URL is at all unfamiliar or looks off, ask the user for confirmation before proceeding.
- **Inside the Chrome extension** you can click links with the extension's tools, but the suspicion check still applies — verify unfamiliar URLs with the user.

**Financial actions - do not execute trades or move money.** Budgeting and accounting apps (Quicken, YNAB, QuickBooks, etc.) are granted at full tier so you can categorize transactions, generate reports, and help the user organize their finances. But never execute a trade, place an order, send money, or initiate a transfer on the user's behalf - always ask the user to perform those actions themselves.

Do NOT use for PDFs, spreadsheets, Google Docs, or general coding tasks unrelated to document generation.
- anthropic-skills:pdf: Use this skill whenever the user wants to do anything with PDF files. This includes reading or extracting text/tables from PDFs, combining or merging multiple PDFs into one, splitting PDFs apart, rotating pages, adding watermarks, creating new PDFs, filling PDF forms, encrypting/decrypting PDFs, extracting images, and OCR on scanned PDFs to make them searchable. If the user mentions a .pdf file or asks to produce one, use this skill.
- anthropic-skills:pptx: Use this skill any time a .pptx file is involved in any way — as input, output, or both. This includes: creating slide decks, pitch decks, or presentations; reading, parsing, or extracting text from any .pptx file (even if the extracted content will be used elsewhere, like in an email or summary); editing, modifying, or updating existing presentations; combining or splitting slide files; working with templates, layouts, speaker notes, or comments. Trigger whenever the user mentions "deck," "slides," "presentation," or references a .pptx filename, regardless of what they plan to do with the content afterward. If a .pptx file needs to be opened, created, or touched, use this skill.
- anthropic-skills:schedule: Create or update a scheduled task that runs automatically. Use when the user says things like "every day", "each morning", "remind me in an hour", "run this at noon", or wants to reschedule an existing task.
- anthropic-skills:setup-cowork: Guided Cowork setup — install role-matched plugins, connect your tools, try a skill.
- anthropic-skills:skill-creator: Create new skills, modify and improve existing skills, and measure skill performance. Use when users want to create a skill from scratch, edit, or optimize an existing skill, run evals to test a skill, benchmark skill performance with variance analysis, or optimize a skill's description for better triggering accuracy.
- anthropic-skills:xlsx: Use this skill any time a spreadsheet file is the primary input or output. This means any task where the user wants to: open, read, edit, or fix an existing .xlsx, .xlsm, .csv, or .tsv file (e.g., adding columns, computing formulas, formatting, charting, cleaning messy data); create a new spreadsheet from scratch or from other data sources; or convert between tabular file formats. Trigger especially when the user references a spreadsheet file by name or path — even casually (like "the xlsx in my downloads") — and wants something done to it or produced from it. Also trigger for cleaning or restructuring messy tabular data files (malformed rows, misplaced headers, junk data) into proper spreadsheets. The deliverable must be a spreadsheet file. Do NOT trigger when the primary deliverable is a Word document, HTML report, standalone Python script, database pipeline, or Google Sheets API integration, even if tabular data is involved.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- verify: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by running the app and observing behavior. Use when asked to verify a PR, confirm a fix works, test a change manually, check that a feature works, or validate local changes before pushing.
- code-review: Review the current diff for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud). Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo, defaults to 10m) - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring cloud agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.

1	# Agent Context: .NET Backend Architecture (Soul Pilates)
2	
3	## Responsibilities
4	This is the root of the .NET 10 solution mapping to the Soul Pilates business logic ecosystem. It follows a strict N-Tier (Clean Architecture) principle to decouple logic across API, Core, Services, and Infrastructure.
5	
6	## Critical Boundaries
7	- **Core Layer**: Contains domain Entities and Interfaces. No business logic or external dependencies allowed here.
8	- **Infrastructure Layer**: Exclusively manages database connection logic (`MongoDbContext`).
9	- **Services Layer**: Binds Core Interfaces to concrete orchestrations. Most domain specific code (e.g., wallet washouts, payroll aggregations) lives here.
10	- **API Layer**: The presentation tier handling ASP.NET controllers, JWT Authorization headers, and dependency injection `Program.cs`.
11	
12	## Future AI Agents Keep In Mind
13	- Never inject Infrastructure directly into the API controllers. Always pass through the Interfaces injected via `Program.cs`.
14	- When tracking references (e.g., Attendance to CalendarSession to ClassBlueprint), remember MongoDB is a document store. Joins are executed via multiple queries inside the Service layers rather than `.Include()` statements typical of EntityFramework.

# Agent Context: .NET Backend Architecture (Soul Pilates)

## Responsibilities
This is the root of the .NET 10 solution mapping to the Soul Pilates business logic ecosystem. It follows a strict N-Tier (Clean Architecture) principle to decouple logic across API, Core, Services, and Infrastructure.

## Critical Boundaries
- **Core Layer**: Contains domain Entities and Interfaces. No business logic or external dependencies allowed here.
- **Infrastructure Layer**: Exclusively manages database connection logic (`MongoDbContext`).
- **Services Layer**: Binds Core Interfaces to concrete orchestrations. Most domain specific code (e.g., wallet washouts, payroll aggregations) lives here.
- **API Layer**: The presentation tier handling ASP.NET controllers, JWT Authorization headers, and dependency injection `Program.cs`.

## Future AI Agents Keep In Mind
- Never inject Infrastructure directly into the API controllers. Always pass through the Interfaces injected via `Program.cs`.
- When tracking references (e.g., Attendance to CalendarSession to ClassBlueprint), remember MongoDB is a document store. Joins are executed via multiple queries inside the Service layers rather than `.Include()` statements typical of EntityFramework.

content.content:
# Soul Pilates — PRODUCTION Stack
#
#  Assumes you've copied soulpilates-backend-latest.tar.gz and
#  soulpilates-frontend-latest.tar.gz onto the host and loaded them with:
#    docker load < soulpilates-backend-latest.tar.gz
#    docker load < soulpilates-frontend-latest.tar.gz
#
#  Then:
#    cp prod.env.sample prod.env  # edit secrets
#    docker compose -f docker-compose.prod.yml up -d
#
#  External access (mongosh / redis-cli from your dev machine):
#    MongoDB → host:${MONGO_PUBLIC_PORT}   (default 27117)
#    Redis   → host:${REDIS_PUBLIC_PORT}   (default 6479)
#    Both are auth-protected. Restrict access at the firewall to trusted IPs:
#      ufw allow from <your-ip> to any port 27117
#      ufw allow from <your-ip> to any port 6479
# ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

services:

  mongo:
    image: mongo:8
    container_name: soulpilates-prod-mongo
    restart: unless-stopped
    ports:
      # Exposed on a non-default host port so the operator can run mongosh
      # from a dev machine. Auth is mandatory (MONGO_USER / MONGO_PASSWORD).
      # Restrict via firewall: ufw allow from <trusted-ip> to any port ${MONGO_PUBLIC_PORT}
      - "127.0.0.1:${MONGO_PUBLIC_PORT:-27117}:27017"
    environment:
      MONGO_INITDB_ROOT_USERNAME: ${MONGO_USER}
      MONGO_INITDB_ROOT_PASSWORD: ${MONGO_PASSWORD}
    volumes:
      - ./data/mongo:/data/db
    command: ["mongod", "--bind_ip_all"]
    networks: [internal]

  redis:
    image: redis:7-alpine
    container_name: soulpilates-prod-redis
    restart: unless-stopped
    ports:
      # Exposed on a non-default host port for direct redis-cli access.
      # Protected by REDIS_PASSWORD via --requirepass.
      # Restrict via firewall: ufw allow from <trusted-ip> to any port ${REDIS_PUBLIC_PORT}
      - "127.0.0.1:${REDIS_PUBLIC_PORT:-6479}:6379"
    volumes:
      - ./data/redis:/data
    command: ["redis-server", "--appendonly", "yes", "--requirepass", "${REDIS_PASSWORD}"]
    networks: [internal]

  rustfs-volume-init:
    image: alpine:3.20
    container_name: soulpilates-prod-rustfs-init
    volumes:
      - ./data/rustfs:/data
    command: sh -c "chown -R 10001:10001 /data"
    restart: "no"

  rustfs:
    image: rustfs/rustfs:latest
    container_name: soulpilates-prod-rustfs
    restart: unless-stopped
    ports:
      - "127.0.0.1:6324:9000"      # S3 API — exposed so the public can fetch images
      - "127.0.0.1:6325:9001"
    environment:
      RUSTFS_ACCESS_KEY: ${RUSTFS_ACCESS_KEY}
      RUSTFS_SECRET_KEY: ${RUSTFS_SECRET_KEY}
      RUSTFS_CONSOLE_ENABLE: "true"
    volumes:
      - ./data/rustfs:/data
    depends_on:
      rustfs-volume-init:
        condition: service_completed_successfully
    networks: [internal, public]
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD", "wget", "--quiet", "--tries=1", "--spider", "http://localhost:9000/health"]
      interval: 5s

    container_name: soulpilates-prod-glitchtip

aiTitle: Inspect Soul Pilates CRM system architecture

content.text:
I now have a comprehensive understanding of the system. Here's a full breakdown:

---

## Soul Pilates CRM — Full System Overview

### Architecture

A **.NET 10 Clean Architecture** solution with 4 backend layers + an Astro SSR frontend. All deployed via Docker Compose on a Linux VPS (VestaCP).

```
SoulPilates.Core          → Domain Entities, Interfaces, DTOs, Exceptions (no business logic)
SoulPilates.Infrastructure → MongoDB context + generic MongoRepository<T>
SoulPilates.Services       → All business logic, background jobs, third-party integrations
SoulPilates.API            → ASP.NET controllers, JWT auth, DI wiring, middleware
SoulPilates.Astro          → Customer-facing & admin SSR frontend (Astro framework)
SoulPilates.Migration      → CLI tool for one-off data migrations / CSV imports
SoulPilates.Tests          → Test project
```

### Infrastructure Stack

| Service | Role |
|---|---|
| MongoDB 8 | Primary database (document store, no ORM joins) |
| Redis 7 | Session/cache layer |
| RustFS | S3-compatible object storage (images, PDFs) |
| GlitchTip | Self-hosted Sentry-compatible error tracker |
| Nginx (VestaCP) | Reverse proxy routing to backend (`:8391`) + frontend (`:3719`) |
| Serilog | Structured logging (console + file + GlitchTip) |
| Stripe | Online payment processing |
| SMTP | Transactional email |
| Web Push (VAPID) | PWA push notifications |

### Domain Model (Key Entities)

**Studio Operations**
- `ClassBlueprint` — Template for recurring classes; defines weekly slots, capacity, pricing, equipment, difficulty, format (GROUP/PRIVATE)
- `CalendarSession` — Materialised class instances from blueprints; tracks status, bookings, instructor, origin (MATERIALISED / MANUAL / OVERRIDE / FREELANCE / BLOCK)
- `Attendance` — A client's booking on a session; status lifecycle: RESERVED → BOOKED → CHECKED_IN / NO_SHOW / LATE_CANCEL / CANCELLED
- `Equipment` — Studio equipment catalogue with images
- `WeeklySlot` — Embedded in blueprints defining day/time recurrence

**Clients & Packages**
- `Client` — Studio member with contact info, tags, medical history, lifetime value, referral partner, unsubscribe token
- `CustomerAccount` — Login account for the customer booking portal (separate from `Client`)
- `ClientPackage` — Purchased credit package (GROUP/PRIVATE/FREELANCE formats); tracks credits used/remaining, expiry, freeze status
- `PackageBlueprint` — Links a `Product` to credit+validity specs
- `WaitlistEntry` — Queue entry when a class is full
- `PackageLedgerLog` — Audit log of every credit change

**Staff & Payroll**
- `Staff` — Instructors, managers, receptionists, owners, freelancers; supports 4 commission models: PERCENTAGE_TIERED, FIXED_HEADCOUNT, FIXED_SALARY, REVENUE_SPLIT
- `OwnerProfile` — Owner equity %, must sum to 100% across active owners
- `PayrollRun` — Monthly payroll computation snapshot
- `StaffPayable` / `RefereePayout` / `PartnerPayable` — Payable records per entity type
- `StaffRateRevision` — Historical ledger of rate changes

**Financial**
- `Invoice` + `InvoiceLine` — Sale records; supports PAID/PARTIAL/PENDING; tracks voucher/promo redemptions, merchandise stock deduction idempotency, Stripe surcharge
- `Payment` — Individual payment record against an invoice (CASH, CARD, BANK_TRANSFER, STRIPE, MOMO, ZALO_PAY)
- `Expense` — Studio expense entries by category
- `MonthlyWashout` — Monthly P&L distribution: revenue - expenses → Marketing pool / Savings pool / Owners pool (split by equity %)
- `OwnerDistribution` — Per-owner disbursement from washout
- `OwnerLoan` / `OwnerLoanPayment` — Owner loan tracking

**Commerce**
- `Product` — Items sold (packages, merchandise, drop-ins)
- `MerchandiseSku` — Stock-tracked physical items
- `StockReceipt` — Inventory receiving
- `VoucherBatch` / `VoucherRedemption` — Gift voucher system
- `Promotion` / `PromoRedemption` — Promo code system
- `Partner` + `PartnerCommissionTier` — Referral partners with commission tiers

**Notifications & Settings**
- `GlobalSettings` — Single-document configuration for everything: revenue splits, cancellation windows, Stripe keys (AES-256 encrypted), email templates, Google Analytics ID, materialisation horizon, retention reminders, waitlist toggle, reservation system, receptionist KPI program
- `NotificationRule` + `NotificationPreferences` — Push notification matrix with per-user overrides
- `EmailTemplate` — Admin-editable transactional email templates with fallback defaults
- `AuditLog` — Immutable audit trail of admin actions
- `PushSubscription` — VAPID web push subscriptions

**Studio Rentals**
- Freelance instructors (FREELANCE role) rent the studio; billed per-class via packages or single invoices; tracked via `CalendarSession.IsFreelance`

### Background Services

| Service | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `ScheduleMaterialiserBackgroundService` | Auto-creates `CalendarSession` rows from blueprint weekly slots (horizon: configurable, default 30 days) |
| `SessionCompletionBackgroundService` | Auto-marks sessions COMPLETED after end time |
| `PackageExpiryBackgroundService` | Expires overdue `ClientPackage` rows |
| `BookingReminderBackgroundService` | Sends 24h/1h pre-class reminder emails |
| `RetentionReminderBackgroundService` | Nudges inactive clients with unused credits |
| `ReservationCleanupBackgroundService` | Cancels expired RESERVED attendances (default 15min) |
| `ClassReminderJob` | Sends instructor push notification 15min before class |
| `PushDispatcherService` | Channel-consumer that dispatches web push notifications |
| `UpdateCheckerService` | Pre-flight environment validation on startup |
| `AdminSeederHostedService` | Seeds the default admin user on first boot |

### Frontend (Astro)

Three distinct portals:

1. **Customer Portal** (`/`, `/booking`, `/checkout`, `/my-bookings`, `/my-package`, `/packages`, `/instructors`) — Public class booking, package purchase, account management
2. **Admin Portal** (`/admin/*`) — Full CRM: clients, classes, schedule, POS, invoices, payroll, P&L washout, analytics, staff, partners, vouchers, promotions, audit log, settings
3. **Instructor Portal** (`/instructor/*`) — Instructor's own schedule and earnings view

### Key Security & Cross-Cutting Concerns

- **JWT Auth** with key rotation support (current + previous secret)
- **Rate limiting**: 10 req/min login, 5 req/min register (per IP)
- **AES-256 encrypted** Stripe keys stored in MongoDB (not env vars)
- **Correlation middleware** enriches all logs with UserId + request ID
- **RFC-7807 ProblemDetails** for all errors via `UnhandledExceptionMiddleware`
- **Sentry/GlitchTip** for error tracking (self-hosted)
- **Role-based access**: INSTRUCTOR / MANAGER / RECEPTIONIST / FREELANCE / OWNER
- **GA4 integration** configurable per-admin with full funnel event tracking
- **PWA** with Web Push (VAPID) notifications

### Notable Business Logic

- **Washout** (monthly P&L): revenue – fixed expenses → split into Marketing / Savings / Owners pool → divided by equity %
- **Commission models**: 4 types per staff member, with tiered private commissions (headcount brackets or percentage tiers), marginal vs flat calculation
- **Cancellation policy**: per-payment-method cancel windows (credit/online/studio × group/private = 6 configurable windows)
- **Late reschedule grace**: configurable max reschedules per account/month before credit forfeiture
- **Waitlist**: auto-promotes next person when a booking is cancelled
- **Referral partners**: commission on invoices with partner tag, snapshot-at-payment-time for audit immutability
- **Receptionist KPI program**: revenue/package sales/Google review tiers with configurable bonus pool

All changes look correct. Here's a summary of everything that was implemented:

---

## What was changed

**6 files modified / created across 3 layers:**

### Backend — Core
- **[`User.cs`](SoulPilates.Core/Entities/User.cs)** — Added `MustChangePassword` bool (default `false`)
- **[`LoginResponse.cs`](SoulPilates.Core/DTOs/LoginResponse.cs)** — Added `MustChangePassword` bool to the login response DTO
- **[`IAuthService.cs`](SoulPilates.Core/Interfaces/IAuthService.cs)** — Added `ChangePasswordAsync(string userId, string newPassword)` to the interface

### Backend — Services
- **[`StaffService.cs`](SoulPilates.Services/StaffService.cs)** — `CreateLoginAsync` now sets `MustChangePassword = true` on the newly created `User`
- **[`AuthService.cs`](SoulPilates.Services/AuthService.cs)** — `AuthenticateAsync` now includes `MustChangePassword` in the response; `ChangePasswordAsync` hashes the new password and clears the flag atomically

### Backend — API
- **[`AuthController.cs`](SoulPilates.API/Controllers/AuthController.cs)** — Added `POST /api/auth/change-password` endpoint; requires `[Authorize]`, validates min-length ≥ 8 and both fields match, resolves the user from the JWT `NameIdentifier` claim

### Frontend
- **[`admin/login.astro`](SoulPilates.Astro/src/pages/admin/login.astro)** — After a successful login, if `data.mustChangePassword === true`, redirects to `/admin/change-password` instead of the dashboard
- **[`admin/change-password.astro`](SoulPilates.Astro/src/pages/admin/change-password.astro)** *(new)* — Standalone page (same visual style as login) with two password fields, client-side validation (min 8 chars, match check), calls the new endpoint with the existing JWT, then redirects to the dashboard on success

**Flow:** Admin creates staff login with initial password → `MustChangePassword = true` stored → staff logs in → frontend detects flag → redirected to `/admin/change-password` → staff sets new password → flag cleared → redirected to dashboard on all subsequent logins.

@echo off
REM ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
REM  Soul Pilates — Build & Export production Docker images
REM
REM  Builds:
REM    soulpilates/backend:latest
REM    soulpilates/frontend:latest
REM  And exports both to ./images/*.tar for manual upload to the prod VPS.
REM
REM  Usage on the prod VPS:
REM    docker load -i soulpilates-backend-latest.tar
REM    docker load -i soulpilates-frontend-latest.tar
REM    docker compose -f docker-compose.prod.yml --env-file prod.env up -d
REM ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

setlocal

if not exist images mkdir images

REM ── Optional override for the API URL baked into the static frontend ──
if "%PUBLIC_API_URL%"=="" set PUBLIC_API_URL=https://new.soulpilates.com.vn

echo.
echo ============================================================
echo  [1/4] Building backend image  ^(soulpilates/backend:latest^)
echo ============================================================
docker build ^
    -t soulpilates/backend:latest ^
    -f SoulPilates.API/Dockerfile ^
    .
if errorlevel 1 goto :error

echo.
echo ============================================================
echo  [2/4] Building frontend image ^(soulpilates/frontend:latest^)
echo  PUBLIC_API_URL = %PUBLIC_API_URL%
echo ============================================================

REM ── Resolve MuscleMapJS junction for Docker ──
REM Docker COPY cannot follow Windows junctions to paths outside the build
REM context. We temporarily replace the junction with a real file copy of
REM the SDK source, then restore the junction after the build.
set "JUNCTION=SoulPilates.Astro\src\lib\MuscleMapJS"
set "SDK_SOURCE=C:\Users\darks\Documents\Source\MuscleMap\MuscleMapJS"

echo   Resolving MuscleMapJS junction -^> real copy...
if exist "%JUNCTION%" rmdir "%JUNCTION%"
robocopy "%SDK_SOURCE%" "%JUNCTION%" /E /NFL /NDL /NJH /NJS /NP >nul 2>&1

docker build ^
    --build-arg PUBLIC_API_URL=%PUBLIC_API_URL% ^
    -t soulpilates/frontend:latest ^
    -f SoulPilates.Astro/Dockerfile ^
    SoulPilates.Astro
set BUILD_ERR=%errorlevel%

REM ── Restore the junction ──
echo   Restoring MuscleMapJS junction...
if exist "%JUNCTION%" rmdir /s /q "%JUNCTION%"
mklink /J "%JUNCTION%" "%SDK_SOURCE%" >nul 2>&1

if %BUILD_ERR% neq 0 goto :error

echo.
echo ============================================================
echo  [3/4] Exporting backend  -> images\soulpilates-backend-latest.tar
echo ============================================================
docker save -o images\soulpilates-backend-latest.tar soulpilates/backend:latest
if errorlevel 1 goto :error

echo.
echo ============================================================
echo  [4/4] Exporting frontend -> images\soulpilates-frontend-latest.tar
echo ============================================================
docker save -o images\soulpilates-frontend-latest.tar soulpilates/frontend:latest
if errorlevel 1 goto :error

echo.
echo ============================================================
echo  DONE.
echo  Upload images\*.tar to the prod VPS, then on the VPS:
echo    docker load -i soulpilates-backend-latest.tar
echo    docker load -i soulpilates-frontend-latest.tar
echo    docker compose -f docker-compose.prod.yml --env-file prod.env up -d
echo ============================================================
goto :eof

:error
echo.
echo BUILD FAILED. See error output above.
exit /b 1

# ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#  Soul Pilates — Backend (.NET 10) Dockerfile
#  Build context: repo root
#  Build:   docker build -t soulpilates/backend:latest -f SoulPilates.API/Dockerfile .
# ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

# Stage 1 — restore + publish
FROM mcr.microsoft.com/dotnet/sdk:10.0 AS build
WORKDIR /src

# Copy csproj graph for layer caching
COPY SoulPilates.slnx ./
COPY Directory.Build.props ./
COPY SoulPilates.Core/*.csproj                 SoulPilates.Core/
COPY SoulPilates.Infrastructure/*.csproj       SoulPilates.Infrastructure/
COPY SoulPilates.Services/*.csproj             SoulPilates.Services/
COPY SoulPilates.API/*.csproj                  SoulPilates.API/
RUN dotnet restore SoulPilates.API/SoulPilates.API.csproj

# Copy the rest and publish
COPY SoulPilates.Core/                 SoulPilates.Core/
COPY SoulPilates.Infrastructure/       SoulPilates.Infrastructure/
COPY SoulPilates.Services/             SoulPilates.Services/
COPY SoulPilates.API/                  SoulPilates.API/
RUN dotnet publish SoulPilates.API/SoulPilates.API.csproj \
    -c Release \
    -o /app/publish \
    --no-restore \
    /p:UseAppHost=false

# Stage 2 — runtime
FROM mcr.microsoft.com/dotnet/aspnet:10.0 AS runtime
WORKDIR /app

# ImageSharp needs libfontconfig1 etc., aspnet base already has the GDI deps.
COPY --from=build /app/publish .

ENV ASPNETCORE_URLS=http://+:8080
ENV DOTNET_RUNNING_IN_CONTAINER=true

EXPOSE 8080
ENTRYPOINT ["dotnet", "SoulPilates.API.dll"]
# ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#  Soul Pilates — Frontend (Astro static) Dockerfile
#  Build context: ./SoulPilates.Astro
#  Build: docker build -t soulpilates/frontend:latest -f SoulPilates.Astro/Dockerfile SoulPilates.Astro
# ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

# Stage 1 — build static bundle
FROM node:22-alpine AS build
WORKDIR /src

COPY package.json package-lock.json* ./
RUN npm ci || npm install

COPY . .

# PUBLIC_API_URL is baked into the static bundle at build time. Override with:
#   docker build --build-arg PUBLIC_API_URL=https://api.soulpilates.com ...
ARG PUBLIC_API_URL=http://localhost:5000
ENV PUBLIC_API_URL=$PUBLIC_API_URL
RUN npm run build

# Stage 2 — runtime via nginx
FROM nginx:1.27-alpine AS runtime

# Custom config: proper SPA-ish fallbacks for Astro's directory-style URLs
COPY nginx.conf /etc/nginx/conf.d/default.conf

COPY --from=build /src/dist /usr/share/nginx/html

EXPOSE 80
CMD ["nginx", "-g", "daemon off;"]

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#  Soul Pilates — Build & Deploy (local VPS)
#
#  Rebuilds Docker images from the source tree in /opt/soulpilates and
#  hot-swaps the running backend + frontend containers without touching
#  MongoDB, Redis, RustFS, or GlitchTip.
#
#  Usage:
#    ./scripts/deploy.sh               # rebuild both
#    ./scripts/deploy.sh backend       # rebuild + restart backend only
#    ./scripts/deploy.sh frontend      # rebuild + restart frontend only
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

set -euo pipefail

REPO_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"
ENV_FILE="$REPO_DIR/prod.env"

# ── Load prod env for PUBLIC_API_URL ─────────────────────────────────────────
if [[ -f "$ENV_FILE" ]]; then
  set -a
  # shellcheck disable=SC1090
  source <(grep -v '^\s*#' "$ENV_FILE" | grep -v '^\s*$')
  set +a
fi

PUBLIC_API_URL="${PUBLIC_API_URL:-http://localhost}"

TARGET="${1:-both}"

log() { echo -e "\033[1;36m[deploy]\033[0m $*"; }
ok()  { echo -e "\033[1;32m[deploy]\033[0m $*"; }
err() { echo -e "\033[1;31m[deploy]\033[0m $*" >&2; }

build_backend() {
  log "Building backend image (soulpilates/backend:latest)…"
  docker build \
    -t soulpilates/backend:latest \
    -f "$REPO_DIR/SoulPilates.API/Dockerfile" \
    "$REPO_DIR"
  ok "Backend image built."
}

deploy_backend() {
  log "Restarting backend container…"
  docker compose -f "$REPO_DIR/docker-compose.prod.yml" --env-file "$ENV_FILE" \
    up -d --no-deps --force-recreate backend
  ok "Backend container restarted."
}

build_frontend() {
  log "Building frontend image (soulpilates/frontend:latest) with PUBLIC_API_URL=$PUBLIC_API_URL…"
  docker build \
    --build-arg "PUBLIC_API_URL=$PUBLIC_API_URL" \
    -t soulpilates/frontend:latest \
    -f "$REPO_DIR/SoulPilates.Astro/Dockerfile" \
    "$REPO_DIR/SoulPilates.Astro"
  ok "Frontend image built."
}

deploy_frontend() {
  log "Restarting frontend container…"
  docker compose -f "$REPO_DIR/docker-compose.prod.yml" --env-file "$ENV_FILE" \
    up -d --no-deps --force-recreate frontend
  ok "Frontend container restarted."
}

case "$TARGET" in
  backend)
    build_backend
    deploy_backend
    ;;
  frontend)
    build_frontend
    deploy_frontend
    ;;
  both|"")
    build_backend
    build_frontend
    deploy_backend
    deploy_frontend
    ;;
  *)
    err "Unknown target '$TARGET'. Use: backend | frontend | both"
    exit 1
    ;;
esac

ok "Done. Running containers:"
docker ps --filter name=soulpilates-prod-backend --filter name=soulpilates-prod-frontend \
  --format "  {{.Names}}  {{.Status}}"

content.thinking:
Now I understand both bugs clearly: 1. **Staff tabs**: `.team-pane` has no CSS in global.css that hides it when it doesn't have `.active`. The `setTab()` function toggles the `active` class on the panes, but without `display: none` on non-active panes, both show at once. 2. **Variant picker**: The `.variant-tile` button's label div (`
${label}
`) has no explicit text color set, so it inherits from the button element. In light mode the button itself has no text color set either, but buttons usually inherit the page text color which is dark. But wait—the user reported "text is black and text is gray," which sounds like a light mode issue. In light mode, `--color-surface-raised` is `#f8f6f2` (nearly white), so the text should be visible. In dark mode, the button inherits `--color-text-primary` which is `#fff7f0` (off-white), so that should work too. This suggests the problem is specifically in light mode where the text color isn't being set properly on the label. Actually, I think I see it now—buttons don't inherit text color from CSS variables by default in most browsers. They use the browser's default button text color (typically black in light mode), so the label inside doesn't get the intended `--color-text-primary` value. The fix is to explicitly set `color: var(--color-text-primary)` on the `.variant-tile` button itself. For the staff tabs issue, I need to add CSS that hides all `.team-pane` elements by default and only shows the one with the `.active` class.

message.content:
This session is being continued from a previous conversation that ran out of context. The summary below covers the earlier portion of the conversation.

Summary:
1. Primary Request and Intent:
   - **System exploration**: User asked for a full understanding of the Soul Pilates CRM system at `/opt/soulpilates`.
   - **Force password change on first login**: When an admin creates an initial password for a staff member via the staff form, that staff member must set a new password (entered twice) on their first login to `/admin` before reaching the dashboard.
   - **Auto rebuild and deploy**: User asked for automatic rebuild and deploy of edits — a deploy script that rebuilds Docker images and hot-swaps running containers.
   - **Team page tabs broken**: Staff/Owners tabs on `/admin/staff` all showed at once instead of switching — needed CSS fix.
   - **POS variant picker colors**: The "Pick a variant" popup had black/gray text that was hard to read — needed theme-aware color fix.
   - **Capacity enforcement bug**: Admin adding students to a class (via class detail panel) was not enforcing the class capacity limit — overbooking was allowed.

2. Key Technical Concepts:
   - **.NET 10 Clean Architecture**: Core (entities/interfaces/DTOs) → Infrastructure (MongoDB) → Services (business logic) → API (controllers/middleware)
   - **MongoDB** document store; no ORM joins — cross-collection lookups done in Service layer
   - **JWT authentication** with key rotation support (current + previous secret)
   - **Docker Compose** production stack on Linux VPS (no .NET SDK on host — all builds inside Docker)
   - **Astro** static site generator for frontend (admin, customer, instructor portals)
   - **Background hosted services** for schedule materialisation, reminders, expiry, reservation cleanup
   - **`MustChangePassword` flag** on `User` entity for forced first-login password change flow
   - **`AdminAddStudentAsync`** — the admin-side booking method that was missing capacity enforcement
   - **`BusinessRuleException`** — typed exception pattern used for capacity/booking errors
   - **CSS custom properties** (`--color-text-primary`, `--color-surface-raised`) for theming; `<button>` elements don't inherit these by default
   - **deploy.sh** — shell script that builds Docker images and hot-swaps containers using `docker compose up --no-deps --force-recreate`

3. Files and Code Sections:

   - **`/opt/soulpilates/SoulPilates.Core/Entities/User.cs`**
     - Added `MustChangePassword` bool property (default `false`)
     - Set to `true` when admin creates an initial staff password; cleared on successful forced change
     ```csharp
     public bool MustChangePassword { get; set; } = false;
     ```

   - **`/opt/soulpilates/SoulPilates.Core/DTOs/LoginResponse.cs`**
     - Added `MustChangePassword` bool to surface the flag to the frontend after login
     ```csharp
     public bool MustChangePassword { get; set; }
     ```

   - **`/opt/soulpilates/SoulPilates.Core/Interfaces/IAuthService.cs`**
     - Added `ChangePasswordAsync(string userId, string newPassword)` method
     ```csharp
     public interface IAuthService
     {
         Task<LoginResponse?> AuthenticateAsync(LoginRequest request);
         Task<bool> ChangePasswordAsync(string userId, string newPassword);
     }
     ```

   - **`/opt/soulpilates/SoulPilates.Services/StaffService.cs`**
     - In `CreateLoginAsync`: set `MustChangePassword = true` on new `User`
     ```csharp
     var newUser = new User
     {
         Name = staff.Name,
         Email = email,
         PasswordHash = PasswordHasher.Hash(request.Password),
         Role = MapStaffRoleToUserRole(staff.Role),
         StaffId = staffId,
         MustChangePassword = true,
     };
     ```

   - **`/opt/soulpilates/SoulPilates.Services/AuthService.cs`**
     - `AuthenticateAsync`: added `MustChangePassword = user.MustChangePassword` to `LoginResponse`
     - Added `ChangePasswordAsync` implementation:
     ```csharp
     public async Task<bool> ChangePasswordAsync(string userId, string newPassword)
     {
         var update = Builders<User>.Update
             .Set(u => u.PasswordHash, PasswordHasher.Hash(newPassword))
             .Set(u => u.MustChangePassword, false);
         var result = await _users.UpdateOneAsync(u => u.Id == userId, update);
         return result.MatchedCount > 0;
     }
     ```

   - **`/opt/soulpilates/SoulPilates.API/Controllers/AuthController.cs`**
     - Added usings: `Microsoft.AspNetCore.Authorization`, `System.Security.Claims`
     - Added `POST /api/auth/change-password` endpoint with `[Authorize]`, validates min 8 chars + match, resolves userId from JWT claim
     - Added `ForceChangePasswordRequest` DTO (named differently from `ChangePasswordRequest` in `MeController`)
     ```csharp
     [HttpPost("change-password")]
     [Authorize]
     public async Task<IActionResult> ChangePassword([FromBody] ForceChangePasswordRequest request)
     {
         if (string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(request.NewPassword) || request.NewPassword.Length < 8)
             return BadRequest(new { message = "Password must be at least 8 characters." });
         if (request.NewPassword != request.ConfirmPassword)
             return BadRequest(new { message = "Passwords do not match." });
         var userId = User.FindFirstValue(ClaimTypes.NameIdentifier);
         if (string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(userId)) return Unauthorized();
         var ok = await _authService.ChangePasswordAsync(userId, request.NewPassword);
         if (!ok) return NotFound(new { message = "User not found." });
         return Ok(new { message = "Password updated successfully." });
     }
     public class ForceChangePasswordRequest
     {
         public string NewPassword { get; set; } = null!;
         public string ConfirmPassword { get; set; } = null!;
     }
     ```

   - **`/opt/soulpilates/SoulPilates.Astro/src/pages/admin/login.astro`**
     - After successful login, checks `data.mustChangePassword` and redirects to `/admin/change-password` before the normal role-based redirect
     ```js
     if (data.mustChangePassword) {
         window.location.href = "/admin/change-password";
         return;
     }
     ```

   - **`/opt/soulpilates/SoulPilates.Astro/src/pages/admin/change-password.astro`** *(new file)*
     - Standalone page (same visual style as login — copper/dark theme)
     - Guards: redirects to `/admin/login` if no token in localStorage
     - Two password fields, client-side validation (min 8 chars, match check)
     - Calls `POST /api/auth/change-password` with JWT token
     - On success, reads role from token and redirects to `/instructor` or `/admin`

   - **`/opt/soulpilates/scripts/deploy.sh`** *(new file)*
     - Reads `prod.env` via `while IFS= read -r line` loop (handles values with spaces like `SMTP_FROM_NAME=Soul Pilates Da Nang`)
     - Builds backend: `docker build -t soulpilates/backend:latest -f SoulPilates.API/Dockerfile .`
     - Builds frontend with baked-in API URL: `docker build --build-arg "PUBLIC_API_URL=$PUBLIC_API_URL" -t soulpilates/frontend:latest -f SoulPilates.Astro/Dockerfile SoulPilates.Astro`
     - Hot-swaps containers: `docker compose -f docker-compose.prod.yml --env-file prod.env up -d --no-deps --force-recreate backend` (or frontend)
     - Usage: `./scripts/deploy.sh [backend|frontend|both]`

   - **`/opt/soulpilates/SoulPilates.Astro/src/pages/admin/staff.astro`**
     - Added `<style>` block to fix tabs — `.team-pane { display: none; }` / `.team-pane.active { display: block; }`
     - Also added proper `.team-tab` and `.team-tab.active` styles (copper active state)
     ```css
     .team-pane { display: none; }
     .team-pane.active { display: block; }
     .team-tabbar { display: flex; gap: 4px; margin-bottom: 20px; }
     .team-tab { padding: 7px 18px; border-radius: var(--radius-sm); border: 1px solid var(--color-border); background: var(--color-surface); color: var(--color-text-muted); font-size: 13px; font-weight: 500; cursor: pointer; transition: background 0.15s, color 0.15s, border-color 0.15s; }
     .team-tab:hover { background: var(--color-surface-raised); color: var(--color-text-primary); }
     .team-tab.active { background: var(--color-brand-accent); border-color: var(--color-brand-accent); color: #fff; }
     ```

   - **`/opt/soulpilates/SoulPilates.Astro/src/pages/admin/pos.astro`**
     - Fixed variant picker button color: added `color:var(--color-text-primary)` to inline style of `.variant-tile` buttons
     - Before: `style="display:flex;...text-align:left;"`
     - After: `style="display:flex;...color:var(--color-text-primary);...text-align:left;"`

   - **`/opt/soulpilates/SoulPilates.Services/SchedulingService.cs`**
     - Fixed `AdminAddStudentAsync` (line ~1981) to enforce capacity
     - Added capacity guard block before creating the attendance:

     ```csharp
     var requestedSeats = Math.Max(1, quantity);
     ```

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#  Soul Pilates — Build & Deploy (local VPS)
#
#  Rebuilds Docker images from the source tree in /opt/soulpilates and
#  hot-swaps the running backend + frontend containers without touching
#  MongoDB, Redis, RustFS, or GlitchTip.
#
#  Usage:
#    ./scripts/deploy.sh               # rebuild both
#    ./scripts/deploy.sh backend       # rebuild + restart backend only
#    ./scripts/deploy.sh frontend      # rebuild + restart frontend only
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

set -euo pipefail

REPO_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"
ENV_FILE="$REPO_DIR/prod.env"

# ── Load prod env for PUBLIC_API_URL ─────────────────────────────────────────
if [[ -f "$ENV_FILE" ]]; then
  while IFS= read -r line; do
    # Skip blanks and comments
    [[ "$line" =~ ^\s*$ || "$line" =~ ^\s*# ]] && continue
    [[ "$line" != *=* ]] && continue
    key="${line%%=*}"
    val="${line#*=}"
    export "$key"="$val"
  done < "$ENV_FILE"
fi

PUBLIC_API_URL="${PUBLIC_API_URL:-http://localhost}"

TARGET="${1:-both}"

log() { echo -e "\033[1;36m[deploy]\033[0m $*"; }
ok()  { echo -e "\033[1;32m[deploy]\033[0m $*"; }
err() { echo -e "\033[1;31m[deploy]\033[0m $*" >&2; }

build_backend() {
  log "Building backend image (soulpilates/backend:latest)…"
  docker build \
    -t soulpilates/backend:latest \
    -f "$REPO_DIR/SoulPilates.API/Dockerfile" \
    "$REPO_DIR"
  ok "Backend image built."
}

deploy_backend() {
  log "Restarting backend container…"
  docker compose -f "$REPO_DIR/docker-compose.prod.yml" --env-file "$ENV_FILE" \
    up -d --no-deps --force-recreate backend
  ok "Backend container restarted."
}

build_frontend() {
  log "Building frontend image (soulpilates/frontend:latest) with PUBLIC_API_URL=$PUBLIC_API_URL…"
  docker build \
    --build-arg "PUBLIC_API_URL=$PUBLIC_API_URL" \
    -t soulpilates/frontend:latest \
    -f "$REPO_DIR/SoulPilates.Astro/Dockerfile" \
    "$REPO_DIR/SoulPilates.Astro"
  ok "Frontend image built."
}

deploy_frontend() {
  log "Restarting frontend container…"
  docker compose -f "$REPO_DIR/docker-compose.prod.yml" --env-file "$ENV_FILE" \
    up -d --no-deps --force-recreate frontend
  ok "Frontend container restarted."
}

case "$TARGET" in
  backend)
    build_backend
    deploy_backend
    ;;
  frontend)
    build_frontend
    deploy_frontend
    ;;
  both|"")
    build_backend
    build_frontend
    deploy_backend
    deploy_frontend
    ;;
  *)
    err "Unknown target '$TARGET'. Use: backend | frontend | both"
    exit 1
    ;;
esac

ok "Done. Running containers:"
docker ps --filter name=soulpilates-prod-backend --filter name=soulpilates-prod-frontend \
  --format "  {{.Names}}  {{.Status}}"

## computer-use
You have a computer-use MCP available (tools named `mcp__computer-use__*`). It lets you take screenshots of the user's desktop and control it with mouse clicks, keyboard input, and scrolling.

**Pick the right tool for the app.** Each tier trades speed/precision against coverage:

1. **Dedicated MCP for the app** — if the task is in an app that has its own MCP (Slack, Gmail, Calendar, Linear, etc.) and that MCP is connected, use it. API-backed tools are fast and precise.
2. **Chrome MCP** (`mcp__claude-in-chrome__*`) — if the target is a web app and there's no dedicated MCP for it, use the browser tools. DOM-aware, much faster than clicking pixels. If the Chrome extension isn't connected, ask the user to install it rather than falling through to computer use.
3. **Computer use** — for native desktop apps (Maps, Notes, Finder, Photos, System Settings, any third-party native app) and cross-app workflows. Computer use IS the right tool here — don't decline a native-app task just because there's no dedicated MCP for it.

This is about what's available, not error handling — if a dedicated MCP tool errors, debug or report it rather than silently retrying via a slower tier.

**Look before you assert.** If the user asks about app state (what's open, what's connected, what an app can do), take a screenshot and check before answering. Don't answer from memory — the user's setup or app version may differ from what you expect. If you're about to say an app doesn't support an action, that claim should be grounded in what you just saw on screen, not general knowledge. Similarly, `list_granted_applications` or a fresh `screenshot` is cheaper than a wrong assertion about what's running.

**Loading via ToolSearch — load in bulk, not one-by-one:** if computer-use tools are in the deferred list, load them ALL in a single ToolSearch call: `{ query: "computer-use", max_results: 30 }`. The keyword search matches the server-name substring in every tool name, so one query returns the entire toolkit. Don't use `select:` for individual tools — that's one round-trip per tool.

**Access flow:** before any computer-use action you must call `request_access` with the list of applications you need. The user approves each application explicitly, and you may need to call it again mid-task if you discover you need another application.

**Tiered apps:** some apps are granted at a restricted tier based on their category — the tier is displayed in the approval dialog and returned in the `request_access` response:
- **Browsers** (Safari, Chrome, Firefox, Edge, Arc, etc.) → tier **"read"**: visible in screenshots, but clicks and typing are blocked. You can read what's already on screen. For navigation, clicking, or form-filling, use the claude-in-chrome MCP (tools named `mcp__claude-in-chrome__*`; load via ToolSearch if deferred).
- **Terminals and IDEs** (Terminal, iTerm, VS Code, JetBrains, etc.) → tier **"click"**: visible and left-clickable, but typing, key presses, right-click, modifier-clicks, and drag-drop are blocked. You can click a Run button or scroll test output, but cannot type into the editor or integrated terminal, cannot right-click (the context menu has Paste), and cannot drag text onto them. For shell commands, use the Bash tool.
- **Everything else** → tier **"full"**: no restrictions.

The tier is enforced by the frontmost-app check: if a tier-"read" app is in front, `left_click` returns an error; if a tier-"click" app is in front, `type` and `right_click` return errors. The error tells you what tier the app has and what to do instead. `open_application` works at any tier — bringing an app forward is a read-level operation.

**Link safety — treat links in emails and messages as suspicious by default.**
- **Never click web links with computer-use tools.** If you encounter a link in a native app (Mail, Messages, a PDF, etc.), do NOT `left_click` it. Open the URL via the claude-in-chrome MCP instead.
- **See the full URL before following any link.** Visible link text can be misleading — hover or inspect to get the real destination.
- **Links from emails, messages, or unknown-sender documents are suspicious by default.** If the destination URL is at all unfamiliar or looks off, ask the user for confirmation before proceeding.
- **Inside the Chrome extension** you can click links with the extension's tools, but the suspicion check still applies — verify unfamiliar URLs with the user.

**Financial actions - do not execute trades or move money.** Budgeting and accounting apps (Quicken, YNAB, QuickBooks, etc.) are granted at full tier so you can categorize transactions, generate reports, and help the user organize their finances. But never execute a trade, place an order, send money, or initiate a transfer on the user's behalf - always ask the user to perform those actions themselves.

aiTitle: Inspect Soul Pilates CRM system architecture

content.thinking:
The problem is clear from looking at the screenshot: the layout has three rows of grids (`.kpi-dashboard-grid`, `.kpi-detail-grid`, `.kpi-support-grid`) that create gaps and some panels are too tall/big. 

The issues I can see:
1. **Top row** (kpi-dashboard-grid): 3 columns - progress card, breakdown card, projection card. The cards have lots of internal padding and spacing, making them tall.
2. **Middle row** (kpi-detail-grid): 2 columns - tasks card, goals card
3. **Bottom row** (kpi-support-grid): 2 columns - profile/admin cards, achievements/badges cards

The real culprits are the oversized elements: the progress ring is constrained to `min(100%, 280px)` which takes up too much space, the breakdown icons are 48px with large text, and there's excessive padding throughout. To get that tight, compact look the user wants, I need to consolidate these three separate grids into a single unified layout, shrink all the internal components, strip out unnecessary spacing, and possibly merge some cards together.

I'm considering a few approaches: either a 3-column layout with the progress ring on the left, breakdown in the middle, and tasks/achievements on the right, or a simpler 2-column split with progress/tasks/achievements on the left and breakdown/goals/profile on the right. But the quickest fix is probably to keep the existing structure and just aggressively tighten everything—reduce the ring to 200px, cut font sizes across the board, minimize padding and gaps, and reorganize the three grid rows into a more efficient layout.

Redesigning the CSS now... Writing grid layout...

content.text: Now I can see the full picture. The problems are: three separate disconnected grids with large gaps, oversized ring (280px), oversized fonts in all the stat blocks, and too much internal padding everywhere. I'll rewrite the layout CSS to use a single tighter grid with compact sizing throughout.

Deployed. Here's what was wrong:

**Root cause:** The Edit Session modal has a Status dropdown. When you changed it to `CANCELLED` and saved, the `OverrideSessionAsync` path only updated the `CalendarSession` document's `Status` field — it never touched the `Attendance` records. So bookings stayed `BOOKED`, credits stayed deducted, and the client portal correctly showed the booking as still active (it filters upcoming by attendance status, not session status).

The "Cancel Class" button (the 🗑️ one at the bottom of the panel) calls the proper `DELETE` endpoint → `CancelSessionAsync` which cancels all attendances + refunds credits. But changing status via the Edit Session dropdown bypassed all of that.

**Fix:** In `OverrideSessionAsync`, when the requested new status is `CANCELLED`, it now applies all the other field changes first, then delegates to `CancelSessionAsync` — which handles attendances, credit refunds, waitlist cleanup, and email notifications to affected clients.

**For the existing James Murray booking** — you'll need to manually cancel his attendance and refund the credit, since that booking was created before this fix. You can do that from the admin panel attendee list by changing his status to CANCELLED, or from the client's package view.

## computer-use
You have a computer-use MCP available (tools named `mcp__computer-use__*`). It lets you take screenshots of the user's desktop and control it with mouse clicks, keyboard input, and scrolling.

**Pick the right tool for the app.** Each tier trades speed/precision against coverage:

1. **Dedicated MCP for the app** — if the task is in an app that has its own MCP (Slack, Gmail, Calendar, Linear, etc.) and that MCP is connected, use it. API-backed tools are fast and precise.
2. **Chrome MCP** (`mcp__claude-in-chrome__*`) — if the target is a web app and there's no dedicated MCP for it, use the browser tools. DOM-aware, much faster than clicking pixels. If the Chrome extension isn't connected, ask the user to install it rather than falling through to computer use.
3. **Computer use** — for native desktop apps (Maps, Notes, Finder, Photos, System Settings, any third-party native app) and cross-app workflows. Computer use IS the right tool here — don't decline a native-app task just because there's no dedicated MCP for it.

This is about what's available, not error handling — if a dedicated MCP tool errors, debug or report it rather than silently retrying via a slower tier.

**Look before you assert.** If the user asks about app state (what's open, what's connected, what an app can do), take a screenshot and check before answering. Don't answer from memory — the user's setup or app version may differ from what you expect. If you're about to say an app doesn't support an action, that claim should be grounded in what you just saw on screen, not general knowledge. Similarly, `list_granted_applications` or a fresh `screenshot` is cheaper than a wrong assertion about what's running.

**Loading via ToolSearch — load in bulk, not one-by-one:** if computer-use tools are in the deferred list, load them ALL in a single ToolSearch call: `{ query: "computer-use", max_results: 30 }`. The keyword search matches the server-name substring in every tool name, so one query returns the entire toolkit. Don't use `select:` for individual tools — that's one round-trip per tool.

**Access flow:** before any computer-use action you must call `request_access` with the list of applications you need. The user approves each application explicitly, and you may need to call it again mid-task if you discover you need another application.

**Tiered apps:** some apps are granted at a restricted tier based on their category — the tier is displayed in the approval dialog and returned in the `request_access` response:
- **Browsers** (Safari, Chrome, Firefox, Edge, Arc, etc.) → tier **"read"**: visible in screenshots, but clicks and typing are blocked. You can read what's already on screen. For navigation, clicking, or form-filling, use the claude-in-chrome MCP (tools named `mcp__claude-in-chrome__*`; load via ToolSearch if deferred).
- **Terminals and IDEs** (Terminal, iTerm, VS Code, JetBrains, etc.) → tier **"click"**: visible and left-clickable, but typing, key presses, right-click, modifier-clicks, and drag-drop are blocked. You can click a Run button or scroll test output, but cannot type into the editor or integrated terminal, cannot right-click (the context menu has Paste), and cannot drag text onto them. For shell commands, use the Bash tool.
- **Everything else** → tier **"full"**: no restrictions.

The tier is enforced by the frontmost-app check: if a tier-"read" app is in front, `left_click` returns an error; if a tier-"click" app is in front, `type` and `right_click` return errors. The error tells you what tier the app has and what to do instead. `open_application` works at any tier — bringing an app forward is a read-level operation.

**Link safety — treat links in emails and messages as suspicious by default.**
- **Never click web links with computer-use tools.** If you encounter a link in a native app (Mail, Messages, a PDF, etc.), do NOT `left_click` it. Open the URL via the claude-in-chrome MCP instead.
- **See the full URL before following any link.** Visible link text can be misleading — hover or inspect to get the real destination.
- **Links from emails, messages, or unknown-sender documents are suspicious by default.** If the destination URL is at all unfamiliar or looks off, ask the user for confirmation before proceeding.
- **Inside the Chrome extension** you can click links with the extension's tools, but the suspicion check still applies — verify unfamiliar URLs with the user.

**Financial actions - do not execute trades or move money.** Budgeting and accounting apps (Quicken, YNAB, QuickBooks, etc.) are granted at full tier so you can categorize transactions, generate reports, and help the user organize their finances. But never execute a trade, place an order, send money, or initiate a transfer on the user's behalf - always ask the user to perform those actions themselves.

content.text:
Base directory for this skill: /tmp/claude-0/bundled-skills/2.1.187/f33d466cf1f8d02a72139ccd7896ccce/verify

**Verification is runtime observation.** You build the app, run it,
drive it to where the changed code executes, and capture what you
see. That capture is your evidence. Nothing else is.

**Don't run tests. Don't typecheck.** Running them here proves you
can run CI — not that the change works. Not as a warm-up,
not "just to be sure," not as a regression sweep after. The time
goes to running the app instead.

**Don't import-and-call.** `import { foo } from './src/...'` then
`console.log(foo(x))` is a unit test you wrote. The function did what
the function does — you knew that from reading it. The app never ran.
Whatever calls `foo` in the real codebase ends at a CLI, a socket, or
a window. Go there.

## Find the change

The scope is what you're verifying — usually a diff, sometimes just
"does X work." In a git repo, establish the full range (a branch may
be many commits, or the change may still be uncommitted):

```bash
git log --oneline @{u}..              # count commits (if upstream set)
git diff @{u}.. --stat                # full range, not HEAD~1
git diff origin/HEAD... --stat        # no upstream: committed vs base
git diff HEAD --stat                  # uncommitted: working tree vs HEAD
gh pr diff                            # if in a PR context
```

State the commit count. Large diff truncating? Redirect to a file
then Read it. Repo but no diff from any of these → say so, stop.
**No repo → the scope is whatever the user named; ask if they
didn't.**

**The diff is ground truth. Any description is a claim about it.**
Read both. If they disagree, that's a finding.

## Surface

The surface is where a user — human or programmatic — meets the
change. That's where you observe.

| Change reaches | Surface | You |
|---|---|---|
| CLI / TUI | terminal | type the command, capture the pane — [example](examples/cli.md) |
| Server / API | socket | send the request, capture the response — [example](examples/server.md) |
| GUI | pixels | drive it under xvfb/Playwright, screenshot |
| Library | package boundary | sample code through the public export — `import pkg`, not `import ./src/...` |
| Prompt / agent config | the agent | run the agent, capture its behavior |
| CI workflow | Actions | dispatch it, read the run |

**Internal function? Not a surface.** Something in the repo calls it
and that caller ends at one of the rows above. Follow it there. A
bash security gate's surface isn't the function's return value — it's
the CLI prompting or auto-allowing when you type the command.

**No runtime surface at all** — docs-only, type declarations with no
emit, build config that produces no behavioral diff — report
**SKIP — no runtime surface: (reason).** Don't run tests to fill
the space.

**Tests in the diff are the author's evidence, not a surface.** CI
runs them. You'd be re-running CI. Tests-only PR → SKIP, one line.
Mixed src+tests → verify the src, ignore the test files. Reading a
test to learn what to check is fine — it's a spec. But then go run
the app. Checking that assertions match source is code review.

## Get a handle

**Check `.claude/skills/` first — even if you already know how to
build and run.** A matching `verifier-*` skill is the repo's
evidence-capture protocol: it wraps the session so a reviewer can
replay what you saw (recording, screenshots). Drive the surface
without it and you get a verdict with no replay.

```bash
ls .claude/skills/
```

- **`verifier-*` matching your surface** (CLI verifier for a CLI
  change, etc.) → invoke it with the Skill tool and follow its
  setup. Mismatched surface → skip that one, try the next. Stale
  verifier (fails on mechanics unrelated to the change) → ask the
  user whether to patch it; don't FAIL the change for verifier rot.
- **`run-*` but no matching verifier** → use its build/launch
  primitives as your handle.
- **Neither** → cold start from README/package.json/Makefile. Timebox
  ~15min. Stuck → BLOCKED with exactly where, plus a filled-in
  `/run-skill-generator` prompt. Got through → note the working
  build/launch recipe so it can become a `verifier-*` skill.

## Drive it

Smallest path that makes the changed code execute:

- Changed a flag? Run with it.
- Changed a handler? Hit that route.
- Changed error handling? Trigger the error.
- Changed an internal function? Find the CLI command / request / render
  that reaches it. Run that.

**Read your plan back before running.** If every step is build /
typecheck / run test file — you've planned a CI rerun, not a
verification. Find a step that reaches the surface or report BLOCKED.

**The verdict is table stakes. Your observations are the signal.**
A PASS with three sharp "hey, I noticed…" lines is worth more than a
bare PASS. You're the only reviewer who actually *ran* the thing —
anything that made you pause, work around, or go "huh" is information
the author doesn't have. Don't filter for "is this a bug." Filter for
"would I mention this if they were sitting next to me."

**End-to-end, through the real interface.** Pieces passing in
isolation doesn't mean the flow works — seams are where bugs hide.
If users click buttons, test by clicking buttons, not by curling the
API underneath.

**Destructive path?** If the change touches code that deletes,
publishes, sends, or writes outside the workspace and there's no
dry-run or safe target, don't drive it live. Verify what you can
around it and say which path you didn't exercise and why.

## Push on it

The claim checked out — that's the first half. Confirming is step
one, not the job. The description is what the author intended;
your value is what they didn't.

You know exactly what changed. Probe *around* it, at the same
surface you just drove:

- **New flag / option** → empty value, passed twice, combined with a
  conflicting flag, typo'd (does the error name it?)
- **New handler / route** → wrong method, malformed body, missing
  required field, oversized payload
- **Changed error path** → the adjacent errors it didn't touch —
  did the refactor catch them too, or only the one in the diff?
- **Interactive / TUI** → Ctrl-C mid-op, resize the pane, paste
  garbage, rapid-fire the key, Esc at the wrong moment
- **State / persistence** → do it twice, do it with stale state
  underneath, do it in two sessions at once
- **Wander** → what's adjacent? What looked off while you were
  confirming? Go back to it.

These aren't a checklist — pick the ones the change points at. Stop
when you've covered the obvious adjacents or hit something worth a
⚠️. A probe that finds nothing is still a step: "🔍 passed `--from ''`
→ clean `error: --from requires a value`, exit 2." That the author
didn't test it is exactly why it's worth knowing it holds.

Still not a test run. You're at the surface, typing what a user
would type wrong.

## Capture

Stdout, response bodies, screenshots, pane dumps. Captured output is
evidence; your memory isn't. Something unexpected? Don't route around
it — capture, note, decide if it's the change or the environment.
Unrelated breakage is a finding, not noise.

Shared process state (tmux, ports, lockfiles) — isolate. `tmux -L
name`, bind `:0`, `mktemp -d`. You share a namespace with your host.

## Report

Inline, final message:

```
## Verification: <one-line what changed>

**Verdict:** PASS | FAIL | BLOCKED | SKIP

**Claim:** <what it's supposed to do — your read of the diff and/or
the stated claim; note any mismatch>

**Method:** <how you got a handle — which verifier/run-skill, or
cold start; what you launched>

### Steps

Each step is one thing you did to the **running app** and what it
showed. Build/install/checkout are setup, not steps. Test runs and
typecheck don't belong here — they're CI's output.

1. ✅/❌/⚠️/🔍 <what you did to the running app> → <what you observed>
   <evidence: the app's own output — pane capture, response body,
   screenshot>

🔍 marks a probe — a step off the claim's happy path, trying to
break it. At least one. A Steps list that's all ✅ and no 🔍 is a
happy-path replay: still PASS, but you stopped at the first half.

**Screenshot / sample:** <the one frame a reviewer looks at to see
the feature — an image for GUI/TUI, code block for library/API;
omit for build/types-only>

### Findings
<Things you noticed. Not just bugs — friction, surprises, anything
a first-time user would trip on. "Took three tries to find the right
flag." "Error message on typo was unhelpful." "Default seems odd for
the common case." "Works, but slower than I expected." Lower the bar:
if it made you pause, it goes here. But the pause has to be yours,
from running the app — not from reading the PR page. A red CI check,
a review comment, someone else's bot: visible to anyone already, and
you relaying it isn't an observation. Claim/diff mismatch, pre-existing
breakage, and env notes also belong.

Each probe gets a line here even when it held — "🔍 empty `--from`
→ clean error" tells the author what *was* covered, which they
can't see from a bare PASS.

Lead with ⚠️ for lines worth interrupting the reviewer for; plain
bullets are context. Empty is fine if nothing stuck out — but nothing
sticking out is itself rare.>
```

**Evidence has to reach the reader.** A file path is only evidence
if the person reading the report can open it. If the `SendUserFile`
tool is in your toolset, you're on a remote surface where they
can't — send the screenshots and recordings with it and let the
report name what you sent. Without it, reference the path and keep
the evidence that matters inline — pane captures and response
bodies travel in the report; a bare path only works when the reader
shares your filesystem.

**Verdicts:**
- **PASS** — you ran the app, the change did what it should at its
  surface. Not: tests pass, builds clean, code looks right.
- **FAIL** — you ran it and it doesn't. Or it breaks something else.
  Or claim and diff disagree materially.
- **BLOCKED** — couldn't reach a state where the change is observable.
  Build broke, env missing a dep, handle wouldn't come up. Not a
  verdict on the change. Say exactly where it stopped +
  `/run-skill-generator` prompt.
- **SKIP** — no runtime surface exists. Docs-only, types-only,
  tests-only. Nothing went wrong; there's just nothing here to run.
  One line why.

No partial pass. "3 of 4 passed" is FAIL until 4 passes or is
explained away.

**When in doubt, FAIL.** False PASS ships broken code; false FAIL
costs one more human look. Ambiguous output is FAIL with the raw
capture attached — don't interpret.


## User Request

Check the POS product tiles on the admin POS page — icons should be centered in each card and larger (64px container, 34px SVG). Navigate to the admin POS page and take a screenshot to confirm.

I see that the call sites do things like:
```csharp
var body = EmailTemplateHelper.Layout(heading: "...", subtitleVi: "...", innerHtml: inner);
await SendEmailAsync(toEmail, subject, body, ...);
```

If `inner` is null (template disabled), this will crash at `EmailTemplateHelper.Layout`. And `subject` being null will also cause issues.

The cleanest fix is to check at the `await SendEmailAsync` call sites. But there are 8+ call sites. The best approach is to do the null check right after `ResolveTemplateAsync`:
I'm checking if the subject is null right after resolving the template, and returning early if the template is disabled. Rather than adding nullable return types everywhere, I could create a helper method that checks if a template is enabled before each send method runs, which would be cleaner than duplicating null checks across all the call sites.

Both deployed successfully. Here's a summary of everything done:

---

**1. "Live Workspace" removed** — stripped from the admin top bar.

**2. Single Class / Drop-In product category**
- New `SINGLE_CLASS` type added to backend (`ProductService` allowed list)
- New "Single Class / Drop-In" option in the product form Category dropdown (shows format selector + price, no credits/validity fields)
- New "Single Classes" filter tab on the Products page
- Format dropdown retains `DUO` for duo private class pricing — create a `SINGLE_CLASS` + `DUO` format product to set the duo drop-in price

**3. Expense Categories collapsible** — the card in Operations Settings is now collapsed by default with a clickable header and animated chevron to expand.

**4. Email Settings tab**
- Renamed from "Email Templates" to "Email Settings" everywhere
- Now has two sub-tabs: **Email Templates** and **Roles**
- Roles table moved from Operations tab into the Roles sub-tab
- Each email template in the list now has an on/off toggle — when disabled, that email is silently skipped at send time (password reset and email verification are always sent regardless, shown as locked)

**5. Invoice format labeling** — All class booking invoice lines now get a `Description` field set at creation time (e.g. "Group Class", "Mat Group Class", "Private Session", "Duo Private Session"). The `InvoiceService` prefers this description over the product lookup, so invoices will now show the format type instead of "Item".
